represents: About 50 minutes (the v2 expansion spans 47 minutes) of API-server audit traffic from the delivery and platform automation of the same staging cluster: Argo CD watching every resource type (Secrets included) and syncing Deployments, ConfigMaps, Services, CronJobs, app Roles/RoleBindings and tenant RoleBindings (team groups bound to edit/view in their namespaces) and pruning closed preview environments; Flux applying node-agent DaemonSets and add-on charts (cert-manager webhook and ClusterRoles, Argo CD's own wildcard ClusterRole); cert-manager cainjector, Gatekeeper's cert-controller and the VPA admission-controller reconciling their Service-backed webhooks; the clusterrole-aggregation-controller re-aggregating admin/edit/view; external-secrets minting Vault-auth tokens and refreshing Secrets; kube-downscaler parking preview Deployments at zero replicas; and CI running `helm upgrade --wait` with pre-upgrade migration hooks, plus preview-namespace teardown: the CI deletes a closed PR's namespace and the namespace controller deletes the collection of every namespaced resource in it (Events included) before finalizing it. Template weights set which behaviours appear and roughly how often relative to each other, not their production rates; treat hits and rate_per_10k as presence indicators, not as production false-positive rates.
provenance: synthetic; event shapes from the audit.k8s.io/v1 Event type, levels per detections/k8s/audit-policy-apiserver.yaml; request bodies modelled on how each tool writes: kubectl client-side apply / Argo CD (strategic-merge diff patch with ?fieldManager=argocd-controller), Flux server-side apply (full apply configuration, ?fieldManager=kustomize-controller&force=true), Helm 3 three-way merge patches (Flux helm-controller too: upgrade.force defaults to false, so no PUT) and release Secrets (sh.helm.release.v1.<name>.v<rev>, owner=helm), the cert-manager v1.15 and Gatekeeper v3.17 chart webhook configurations (Gatekeeper's validation webhook ships failurePolicy Ignore), VPA's delete-then-create self-registration, the bootstrap edit/admin/view ClusterRoles, kube-downscaler's pykube-ng update(), which sends the whole listed Deployment (replicas and the original-replicas annotation changed) as a JSON merge patch; the namespace controller's teardown sweep per pkg/controller/namespace/deletion (discovery, then DeleteCollection with propagationPolicy Background, or list and delete for resources without it, a verifying list, status conditions and /finalize), written as one sequence with an audit ID per request. CA bundles are random bytes in a PEM envelope, not certificates. Version strings are illustrative; names are fictional; addresses RFC1918.
